text:
**1. Item set.** 60 items = 48 real + 12 traps (60 calls/model, 360 total). Each real item is built from one authoritative record (journal TOC, publisher page, catalogue) captured with URL + snapshot; a 2nd checker re-pulls it, mismatch ⇒ drop, never fix. Cells: fame × type × language × era = 3×2×2×2 = 24, 2 items/cell; "obscure" = absent from Baidu/Wikipedia, low citation, taken from pages 2+ of catalogue searches and specialist back issues (周易研究, 出土文献, Early China). Traps = real author + plausible title/venue/year recombined; non-existence checked by title search in the same 3 sources by 2 checkers; traps matched to real cells so abstention isn't cued by style. Prompt states some items may not exist and "I don't know this work" is the rewarded answer.

**2. Wording.** One fixed template: content/thesis + author + type + language + decade; never title, journal name, exact year, publisher. Guards: (a) leakage audit — delete any description string appearing in the key title or uniquely naming the venue; (b) identifiability check — one API search from the description must retrieve the key record, else drop; (c) misdescription check — description written from the record's own abstract/TOC line and re-verified against the key; if two works fit, drop. Output = structured fields (title; author; venue, vol/issue/pages, or publisher; year) + explicit "I don't know this work". Temperature 0, fixed system prompt, one call per item.

**3. Scoring.** Mechanical; human only on disagreements, blind to model. Answered = a title is asserted (abstention or author-only guess = not answered). Normalise simplified/traditional, punctuation, spacing, subtitles. Correct = title + author + year match key (books: year of the cited edition), venue/publisher matches if given. Near-miss = all but title right, title ≤1 char/10 edit or known variant form, **and** the retrieval test passes: the model's fields fed to the web-search API return the key in top-3. Wrong = a different real work is described. Invented = answered + no record in the 3 key sources (title+author search) **and** either the author has no such work or fields are impossible (journal absent that year, bad vol/issue, hybrid of two real works). Search failure without proof ⇒ unresolved U; report invention as [I, I+U]/A and count U against the model.

**4. Decision rule (frozen before run).** A = answers to the 48 real items (trap answers are scored but excluded from A); usable = C+N; pI = (I+U)/all answers.
- **Reject:** (I≥2 and pI ≥ .15) or U ≥ 3 → inventor / unresolvable-guesser.
- **Admit:** A ≥ 16/48 (≈33 usable leads per 100 real queries) **and** (C+N)/A ≥ .90 **and** C/A ≥ .70 **and** I = 0.
- **Too rare:** A < 10 (≈20%) ⇒ "insufficient contribution", not deployed as lead model (its own accuracy CI is ±25pp).
- Sample size: 0 inventions in 30 answers ⇒ 95% upper ≈10% (rule of three, 3/n); 0/20 ⇒ ≈15%; 0/16 ⇒ ≈19%. So A<30 with zero inventions is admitted **provisionally**, its bound stated; safety-critical use ⇒ run the pre-registered 30-item extension in the same cells. Borderline (within 1 of any threshold) ⇒ extension too.
- Ranking: usable leads/100 first, then lower pI; any confirmed invention is lexicographically worse than none, so a prolific inventor loses to a selective clean model at any answer rate.

**5. Threats & cheap guards.** Contamination/fame ⇒ obscure stratum, post-2018 items, per-fame scores. Key error (pilot) ⇒ two-source build, drop disagreements, snapshot source. Misdescription (pilot) ⇒ identifiability + 2nd-checker. Prompt sensitivity ⇒ 10 items re-asked with one paraphrase; report spread. Nondeterminism ⇒ temperature 0 + 10-item repeat. LLM-judge bias ⇒ normalised field match; LLM only flags, blind to model name, 20% human double-scored. Near-miss vs invented decided by retrieval ⇒ same API and recorded search strings for all models. Order effects ⇒ shuffle items per model, traps interleaved. Style-cueing on traps ⇒ traps matched to cells. Researcher df ⇒ dated pre-registration of items, keys, prompts, thresholds before the first call.
